name: Contingent-workforce identity controls with enforceable supplier governance

attribution.legal_posture: This is private supplier policy and guidance, not a statute, regulation, or adjudication, and it supplies no evidence that Salesforce experienced an incident.

caveats: Evidence class: first-party supplier requirements describing controls; incident status belongs to a separate evidence class.

Generalize the control for other organizations; Salesforce incident attribution requires source evidence. Keep private identity documents out of reproduction and requests. Require lawful, proportionate, accessible verification with human review and anti-discrimination safeguards.
Guidance and prospective scenarios are presented as guidance, while source-reported suspicion remains distinct from adjudicated fact.
Legal-status boundary: private contractual governance guidance; its scope is contractual, with statute, regulation, adjudication, and Salesforce incident disclosure outside it.
Nationality, accent, language, appearance, geography, camera behavior, remote-work preference, job title, and any single technical signal require corroboration before attribution or adverse action.
Unnamed organizations and people remain unidentified in the source record.
Use proportionate, documented, privacy-preserving review with a meaningful human appeal path.

infrastructure.statement: Salesforce's contingent-workforce supplier enablement ties layered interview, identity, background and change-request checks to supplier governance: intentional failure to adhere to and adapt the guidance may trigger business review and possible contract termination. The useful cross-sector lesson is to make identity-continuity controls flow down to staffing and contingent-labor suppliers and to establish an enforceable exception and escalation path.
infrastructure.evidence_class: first-party supplier requirements, not an observed incident
infrastructure.sector: public-sector, regulated-sector and critical-infrastructure procurement supply chains

sources.support: Salesforce directs contingent-workforce suppliers to implement available measures against inauthentic candidates associated with the DPRK IT-worker scheme. It requires layered interview and identity checks, escalation of cross-platform inconsistencies, direct verification of employment and education, scrutiny of abrupt identity or work-location changes, and states that intentional failure to adhere to and adapt the guidance may trigger business review and possible contract termination. Evidence class: supplier governance and hiring guidance, not an incident disclosure Legal-status boundary: Private supplier policy and guidance; not proof that Salesforce hired or was compromised by a DPRK IT worker.
